correctness.rationale: The 2026 primary source proves for arbitrary real normed spaces that locally finite tilability is equivalent to admitting an equivalent norm that is both \(K\)-polyhedral and LFC. Restrict such a norm to a linear subspace \(Y\). Every finite-dimensional \(E\subseteq Y\) is also a finite-dimensional subspace of \(X\), so the restricted unit-ball section is the same polytope. LFC is inherited by intersecting the witnessing neighborhood with \(Y\) and restricting the finitely many continuous functionals. Equivalent-norm constants also restrict unchanged. Applying the same characterization to \(Y\) proves the statement without completeness or closedness assumptions.
correctness.risk: The result is existential and gives no relationship between the ambient tiles and a subspace tiling.
